setting.note: A bookish young woman with a head full of Gothic novels comes to fashionable Bath for the season, learns to read people rather than plots, and is then carried off to a real abbey where she must tell her lurid imaginings from the truth.

rights.originalWork: Written in the late 1790s, published posthumously 1817. Jane Austen died in 1817; the work is in the public domain. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of the text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: Northanger Abbey, Jane Austen (1817). Locations mapped by Read the Places; not affiliated with or endorsed by any estate or publisher.

palette.note: A muted plum, half Gothic gloom and half drawing-room fashion, for a book that plays one against the other. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
